本月最重要文章，没有之一

quotedTweet.text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++
More comprehensive analysis: https://t.co/vaTuiyyYB6

Found out the hard way (again) that you can't use a Codex reset whenever you want.

I had a full reset (weekly + 5 hour) expiring tonight at 12:58 AM, and I'd already used 82% of my week. So I tried to use it before it disappeared.

Codex said "Your usage does not need a reset right now"

Turns out OpenAI only lets you use it when you've hit your limit or you're very close. 

So basically I just lost one. Guess I was too busy with Opus 5.5 and GLM to burn enough Codex tokens to deserve it.

text:
openai has been working on the research behind dots for almost two years.

most people assumed this was a response to other labs.

It wasn't the thing that took two years wasn't making it smart, it was making it remember.

→ dots stay coherent over weeks. you teach it your preferences once, it doesn't forget the brief two weeks later.

→ they never stop. if there's nothing useful to do, they sleep. the moment something comes up, they wake back up.

→ they run long-horizon tasks across multiple days without losing track

every other agent today resets context after a conversation ends. dots don't have conversations. they have ongoing relationships with your work.

that's what took two years to build.

openai has been working on the research behind dots for almost two years.

most people assumed this was a response to other labs.

It wasn't the thing that took two years wasn't making it smart, it was making it remember.

→ dots stay coherent over weeks. you teach it your preferences once, it doesn't forget the brief two weeks later.

→ they never stop. if there's nothing useful to do, they sleep. the moment something comes up, they wake back up.

→ they run long-horizon tasks across multiple days without losing track

every other agent today resets context after a conversation ends. dots don't have conversations. they have ongoing relationships with your work.

that's what took two years to build.

终于有人把自己做交易终端最麻烦的 K 线图层，做成了一套够轻、够完整的开源底座。

KLineChart，4.2K Stars，Apache-2.0 开源，零依赖、Gzip 只有约 40KB 的专业金融图表库。

以前做行情界面，最烦的就是手写 K 线图：蜡烛、均线、成交量、画线工具……一套下来又大又卡。

KLineChart 不一样，HTML5 Canvas 写的轻量 K 线图，零第三方依赖、gzip 才 40K，内置多指标加画线模型，一个图表多端适配，TypeScript 类型全给你。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 零依赖 + 轻量：Gzip 约 40KB，拿来做网页和桌面金融终端都很顺

2️⃣ 指标 + 画线：内置多种指标和 Overlay，也支持自己扩展指标、图形和标注

3️⃣ 实时数据接口：历史加载、实时更新、向前补数据、切 Symbol / Period 都能自己控制

4️⃣ v10 多 Y 轴：同一个 Pane 可以挂不同指标、不同坐标轴，复杂图表更好搭

5️⃣ 高度可定制：主题、坐标轴、Tooltip、快捷键、Crosshair、缩放逻辑都能自己改

6️⃣ 移动端也支持：一套图表可以同时适配 PC 和手机，不用重新做一套

我觉得它最值钱的地方，不是“能画 K 线”。

而是你想自己做量化终端、行情网站、AI Trading Dashboard，最基础也最容易耗掉大量开发时间的图表层，它已经帮你铺好了。

上面再接自己的行情、指标、策略、AI Agent，基本就能继续往 TradingView 风格终端方向搭。

做股票量化、Crypto 看盘、金融前端或者交易终端的，这个很适合收藏。

https://t.co/r0hxGhJy63

quotedTweet.text:
离谱！港大实验室把一支迷你量化对冲基金，直接开源 了

Vibe-Trading，34K+ Stars，MIT 开源，一套能自己找数据、挖因子、跑回测、组 Agent 团队的金融研究平台。

以前做一个量化策略，要自己找数据、写因子、选回测引擎、调参数、看结果，整个流程全靠人一点点拼。

Vibe-Trading 不一样，你只需要用自然语言说想研究什么，剩下的数据、因子、回测、Agent 分工，它自己往下跑。

核心能力：

1️⃣ 90 个 Finance Skills：行情、期权、因子、回测、研究工具都能直接让 Agent 调用

2️⃣ 462 个现成 Alpha：Qlib158、Alpha101、GTJA191、学术因子、基本面因子都已经整理好

3️⃣ 10+ 回测引擎：A 股、全球股票、Crypto、期货、外汇、期权等多个市场都能直接测

4️⃣ 30 个 Swarm Teams：投资委员会、Quant Desk、Risk Review、Macro、Crypto 等团队可以直接拉起来协作

5️⃣ Persistent Memory：过去研究、Session、Skills 和上下文可以继续保留，不用每次从零开始

6️⃣ Shadow Account：上传自己的 Broker Journal，AI 可以反推你的交易模式，再做反事实回测和审计

我觉得它最有意思的地方，是 AI 终于不只是“回答金融问题”。

而是开始真正执行一条研究链：

你提问题，它自己找数据、做分析、跑回测、拉 Agent 开会，最后把研究结果交回来。

以前要一桌量化研究员干的活，现在开始变成一句话启动。

做 AI 量化、股票研究、Crypto、因子挖掘，或者想把 Agent 真正接进投研流程的，这个很值得收藏。

https://t.co/SG1plmW9TZ

we're seeing our coding agent costs decrease significantly for second month in row

text:
AI Drug Discovery Is Becoming a Bottleneck Trade

I get excited when an industry starts going through a real regime change. AI drug discovery (“AIDD”) increasingly looks like one of those moments.

Two things are happening:
1/ Upstream: the frontier AI labs are piling in.
2/ Downstream: The supply chain is clearly moving.

Supply-chain checks suggest the upstream picks-and-shovels of discovery and early preclinical R&D are starting to feel the increase in experimental volume.

DNA → protein → assays → sequencing → automation → preclinical testing

Names across that stack include $TWST , @GenScript , $ILMN , $TXG , lab-automation vendors and CROs.

$TWST expects triple-digit percentage growth in AI-enabled drug-discovery orders in FY26, and another year of triple-digit order growth in FY27.

@GenScript's AIDD business doubled YoY in 1H26. Its current platform advertises industrial-scale validation of 4,000+ designs/day, with integrated sequence-to-data workflows. Our channel checks suggest the ramp is moving even faster: roughly 8,000 designs/day currently, with a path toward ~16,000/day by YE26.

---
Why does AI drive more wet-lab demand?

1/ AI makes hypothesis generation almost free → way more shots on goal.
The bottleneck is moving from expert-driven design to biological validation.

2/ AI models need continuous experimental feedback — and both good and bad data are useful.
Traditionally, only the highest-conviction A+ candidates might get pushed into expensive validation. With AI, even the B/C candidates can be valuable because failed experiments generate training data.

@GenScript has said its sequence-to-binding workflow can return data in 4–7 days, and that faster cycle times matter because AI models depend on continuous experimental feedback.

@Anthropic is a clean example. @claudeai  designed 1,320 protein binders. @adaptyvbio  converted those digital sequences into DNA, expressed the proteins and tested binding. Only 354 actually bound. And the 966 failures are not wasted. They are useful negative labels: what does not express, what does not bind, what has poor affinity. Those results help train the next model iteration.

3/ Wet labs are no longer just making drugs. They are making training data.
$TWST  / @GenScript  increasingly look like biological data foundries.

$TWST explicitly talks about generating model-ready data from AI-designed sequences. In some workflows, the customer may care less about receiving the physical protein than about getting structured experimental results back into the model.

Traditional drug discovery asks: “Does candidate X work?”

AI drug discovery also asks: “What can this experiment teach the model?”

---
TAM of AIDD

If AI is simply a better R&D tool, the relevant spending pool is the $300–400B of annual global pharma R&D. If AI meaningfully increases the number of viable drug programs, the opportunity is larger because it expands downstream demand for DNA synthesis, protein production, assays, and preclinical work.

Near term, we can also size demand from AI-company spending. If Anthropic reaches $80B of ARR in 2026 and spends just 1% on AIDD, that alone would imply ~$800M of annual investment.

---
Trade setup

This is a trade that could have long legs. It’s hard to really stop working until PhaseI/II results (2028+)

It smells a lot like the bottleneck trade we just saw in semis: GPUs → HBM → networking → power/cooling. In biology, It basically follows the drug discovery process downstream: AI models → designs → DNA/protein → assays → preclinical capacity.

After the upstream picks-and-shovels, animal testing could become the next bottleneck. Monkey prices are already near prior highs and CRO capacity is tight. AIDD pushing more candidates into preclinical development would only add demand.

?? But clinical trials are still the bottleneck?
This is the biggest pushback I keep coming back to. No matter how fast discovery becomes, drugs still need to go through preclinical → Phase I → Phase II → Phase III → approval. You still need patients, time and capital.

But that doesn’t mean the bottleneck trade won’t work. More viable candidates — especially with higher success rates — still means more demand throughout the development process.

And who knows: clinical trials themselves may eventually be optimized by AI.

?? What breaks the trade?
Near term, the picks-and-shovels trade breaks if experimental budgets stop growing, AI-generated designs don’t translate into useful wet-lab hits, or capacity catches up too quickly.

Longer term, the thesis breaks if AI drugs look great in discovery / Phase I but fail at normal rates in Phase II/III. That is why Phase II matters so much.

?? Milestones
Late 2026–2027: first Isomorphic-designed drugs enter human trials; more AI-native programs move into IND-enabling work / tox.

2028–2030: clinical trial results start telling us whether AI-designed drugs actually perform better than conventional drugs.

Calling all the "bottleneck bros". :) @jukan05 @zephyr_z9 @aleabitoreddit @ParadisLabs 

+++
More comprehensive analysis: https://t.co/vaTuiyyYB6

Use a warm off-white canvas, black UI and iOS 26 liquid glass over the photos. Archivo (wdth 125, weight 800) for the wordmark, Geist for the UI. A cursor triggers every change with actual clicks, drags and long-presses. Zoom the camera screen-studio style so each moment fills the square, and scale the cursor with it.
Banned: crossfades, blur-ins, brightness "developing", 3D flips, particles, glows, holds longer than 1s, anything that feels like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
120 BPM, 54 beats, with something happening on every beat.
Open: the wordmark compresses into its own period like an accordion. The dot expands into a black pill, and a label rises inside it. Click: six iris blades close over the label, then snap open onto a photo. The circle turns into a square and shrinks. A grid unfolds behind it like a paper map (center, plus, corners), rearranges into a bento, and a click zooms into one tile, landing right on the drop.
Glass: a glass word appears letter by letter, then melts into a droplet that stretches into a glass toolbar. The adjust icon turns it into a slider. Dragging changes the photo lighting from day to golden hour (two aligned shots), while the held knob becomes a glass lens. It rises into a glass orb, the next photo opens inside it as a circle, and the orb grows into a lock screen with glass clock digits, a date and a home bar that stretches into a glass music player.
Stage: the lock screen pulls back to reveal a phone, with the bezel growing from the screen edge. The Dynamic Island stretches like liquid, pinches off, flies across and expands into a Mac window that rolls up like a blind. Long-press the wallpaper and drag it onto a Safari tab. The page pushes in; when you drop the image, it becomes the hero of a landing page. Scroll: the hero transforms into a framed print on a product card, with the mat and molding growing from the photo's edge. Choose a frame color (it paints across) and a size, then the nav button flies down and becomes "Order print".
Order: one black shape keeps changing: Ordered ✓ → Printing % → On its way (a van on a route) → Delivered ✓.
Wall: the delivered circle expands until black fills the frame, holds for one beat, then shrinks into the framed print hanging in the real wall footage. The same iris opens onto the print and closes again. The frame fills the screen, contracts into the pill → the dot → the letters spring back out on the returning beat. Last frame = first frame.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, square 1440x1440. Compute every style from time inside an async seek(t): no CSS transitions, timers or state carried between frames.
2. Use closed-form step responses for springs. When a value has multiple targets, add one spring per change so it remains a pure function of time.
3. Liquid glass: each glass element keeps its own clone of the scene behind it. Filter that clone with an SVG feImage displacement map (a rounded-rect distance field) through three feDisplacementMaps at slightly different scales for chromatic edges, then add a rim light. For glass letters, use a canvas distance field per glyph to create the map, mask and highlights.
4. Goo: apply blur and an alpha threshold, then composite the source on top so the glass stays sharp inside.
5. Iris: place 6 blades around a hexagonal aperture. Each blade uses its two vertices, both edge extensions and the SHORT arc between them.
6. Wordmark squeeze: move every letter toward the dot by the same factor and adjust its drawn width to match (narrow the wdth axis, scale the rest), keeping the letters in contact.
7. Footage: re-encode it all-intra (ffmpeg -g 1), load it as a blob URL and await "seeked" before drawing each frame.
8. Sound: use a downloaded SFX for every event (Mixkit), never synthesized, and position each by its measured peak. Start the song on a downbeat: land the zoom on the drop, place the wall in the breakdown and bring back the wordmark with the beat. Loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
9. Render with Playwright: blend 4 subframes per frame using ffmpeg tmix at 60fps. Check one frame per beat, then look for single-frame pops (frame-difference spikes 3x higher than their neighbours).

<gotchas>
backdrop-filter: url() misreads displacement maps in Chromium, so clone the scene instead. A flood needs to extend beyond the corners and take about 0.3s; otherwise, half the screen changes in a single frame. A child set to visibility: visible can show through a hidden parent, so use inherit. Text swapping inside a morphing shape needs its own mask. python http.server can't range-seek video, so use the blob URL.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the beat map and 4 stills (open, glass, stage, wall) before writing the full film.
</start>

text:
卧靠，这个有点颠覆认知了！
运动哪里是为了减肥啊，人家真正的作用，是给大脑“充电”！

有一种叫海鞘的生物，小时候像小蝌蚪一样游来游去，有完整的大脑，可一旦找到地方定居下来，就会把自己的大脑吃掉！因为它再也不用动了，大脑对它来说就是个“奢侈品”——占体重才2%，却要消耗30%的热量，太不划算了。

你看，这像不像现在的我们？上班坐着、下班躺着，能不动就不动，结果大脑也跟着“躺平”了。可你知道吗？大脑天生就是为运动而生的！你动得越多，大脑就越活跃，还会分泌一种叫BDNF的“脑源性神经营养因子”，相当于给脑神经细胞“施肥”，让神经元连接更紧密，信息传递更快，记忆力、专注力、逻辑思维能力直接拉满。

深圳有个针对两万多名中学生的研究，结果特别扎心：运动频率越高，语数英成绩越好！每周运动三次以上的孩子，语文成绩好的概率高出31%，数学高出28%，英语更是高出35%！这哪里是在练身体，明明是在给大脑“升级”啊！

还有个更颠覆的真相：我们以前总以为大脑到24岁就定型了，30岁以后只会走下坡路。但最新的脑科学研究早就打脸了，大脑的可塑性是终身的！你30岁学新技能、40岁坚持运动、50岁接触新事物，大脑都会不断“重塑”自己，越用越灵活。

视频里有句话我特别认同：“肌肉是大脑的化工厂”。你做抗阻训练、有氧运动，肌肉就会产生各种神经营养因子，源源不断地送到大脑里。所以你看那些CEO、大学教授、政治家，再忙都要抽时间运动——不是他们精力太旺盛，是他们知道：不运动，一天都撑不下来！

所以兄弟姐妹们，别再等“有空再运动”了，也别纠结“做什么运动好”。先动起来！哪怕每天快走30分钟，哪怕在家做几组简单的力量训练，只要你开始动，大脑就会开始“长脑子”。

(视频资料来源：抖音 嗨咻HiShow)

text:
A week of Claude Code sessions is too much to remember. Every weekend, have Opus 5.5 vibe-code a quick 𝘄𝗲𝗲𝗸𝗹𝘆 𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗮𝗿 like this from your local session logs.

Then give it 𝗮 𝘀𝘂𝗯𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝘀 𝘄𝗲𝗲𝗸𝗹𝘆 𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗮𝗿𝘀:
→ Name it week-calendar, set its effort to medium, and preload a design skill
→ The first time, it asks which colors you like and whether to color by project or by task, and saves that to memory. After that, every calendar follows it
→ Call it when you want to look back on the week or write a weekly report. It regenerates the calendar and writes up a 3-line weekly report for you
→ The calendar shows four things: when you worked each day, what each session did, 𝘄𝗵𝗶𝗰𝗵 𝘀𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗽𝗽𝗲𝗱 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗮 𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴𝗹𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗶𝘁, and how many hours each project took this week

Send this prompt to Claude Code 👇

"Set up a subagent that only builds weekly calendars:

1. Create week-calendar in ~/.claude/agents: model: opus, effort: medium, memory: user. Preload the design skills I have installed (for example impeccable). Give it Bash so it can run git log and the script that builds the calendar. It only writes files to ~/.calendar/ and its own memory.
2. The first time, it asks me what style I like: dark or light, one accent color, color by project or by task type, and whether the week starts on Monday or Sunday. It saves my answers to memory and follows them every time.
3. The calendar is one HTML file. The script writes the data straight into it, so it opens with a double-click. Use this week's session logs: Claude Code's are in ~/.claude/projects/ (skip the subagents folders), and if I use Codex, add ~/.codex/sessions/. Before writing the script, open one file to check the fields. Convert times to my local time zone, and use the cwd in each record to tell projects apart. One block per session; start a new block after any gap longer than 30 minutes. Clicking a block shows the project, start and end time, the model used, the session title (if there isn't one, sum up my first typed message in 3 to 5 words), my first typed message, and my commits and changed files in that repo during that time (skip folders that aren't git repos). Sessions that stopped without a single commit get a red outline and also go in a separate list. At the top, total this week's hours per project, counting parallel sessions only once. Keep everything local.
4. Add a rule to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: when I say "what did I do this week" or "write my weekly report", have week-calendar regenerate the calendar first, then write a 3-line weekly report from it: what I mainly got done this week, which project took the most time, and which no-commit sessions to pick up first next week.

Show me the contents of the files you'll create or change, then explain the whole flow in words a 10-year-old could follow. Don't write anything until I confirm."

text:
周一还没开盘，期货要到周日晚6点（美东）才恢复交易

趁周末我先把消息翻了一遍
理一下开盘的线索

//

周五收盘定的调子很重要，因为周一早盘大概率是接着这个定价走

9月非农只加了2.9万个岗位，预期大概 9 万

差了一大截
失业率 4.2%

市场的反应是
10 月加息的可能性被大幅压低，有口径从之前将近七成直接掉到24%左右

但股市没跌
道指+0.49%，标普+0.73%，纳指 +1.19%，纳斯达克 100 收盘创了新高

逻辑很简单：就业弱 → 加息概率低 → 成长股受益
教科书式的弱非农交易

//

周五个股留了三条线，周一开盘我会先看这几个

英伟达收 233.95，盘中摸到 237.88，5 月以来首次创盘中新高

半导体整体偏强，但存储反着走
东芝说要扩产硬盘，希捷和西部数据各跌了大概 10%

扩产消息对存储股是利空，产能上来价格就压下去了

特斯拉 +4.65%
Q3 交付 486532 辆，比预期的 46.4 万高了不少
SpaceX 也涨了 7.35%

耐克是道指表现最差的之一，跌了大概 3.6%
中国需求的问题，加上全年收入指引下修

━━━━━

周一白天真正能改变定价的只有一个东西：早上10点的 9 月 ISM 服务业 PMI，预期 55.1 左右，前值 55.4

标题数字无所谓
关键看里面的分项

新订单如果还在扩张、物价分项还高，周五那套暂停加息的交易逻辑就要被打回去

但如果就业分项也跟非农一样转弱，成长股和中小盘大概率继续跑

说白了就是两个剧本，ISM出来之前都是猜

9:45还有标普全球服务业 PMI 终值，当天没有重要财报

中国国庆假到 10 月7号，亚太流动性薄
美联储会议纪要在周三，跟周一没关系
周一就看那一个数

不作投资建议，DYOR
#美股 #半导体

最让我注意的是回购

未来几个月计划回购大约10亿美元股票，之后最高把50% 的自由现金流拿来回购

对一家EDA 公司来说，这个信号很重

以前这类公司更喜欢把钱砸进研发和收购，现在愿意拿一半自由现金流还给股东，说明管理层觉得自己被低估了。

2027财年营收目标同比增长15%，也上调了

AI 芯片设计越复杂，EDA 工具越不可能被换掉

新思和 Cadence 基本上垄断了这条链路

但我关心的不是AI 受益这个标签
谁都在贴

我关心的是回购力度，因为这代表管理层对自由现金流的信心，不是讲故事，是拿真金白银在投票。

text:
用 AI 写代码越来越屎山，大概率是因为大模型的默认生成偏好。

大语言模型本质是代码生成器，在海量开源代码训练出来的直觉里，倾向于建立抽象、引入通用依赖和堆叠包装层。
只要跟它说加个弹窗，它很自然地去装第三方组件库，补齐配套的样式与封装，给简单的需求挂上一整套外部依赖。
但在真实工程里，维护成本往往跟代码量成正比，多一个依赖就多一层版本冲突和安全风险。

有个叫 ponytail 就是解决这个问题的，核心思路是在 Agent 动笔之前强制插入一套优先级梯子。

遇到任务不急着写新逻辑，先顺着梯子逐级排查：
第一层先按 YAGNI 原则确认需求必要性，没有明确要求的不做。
第二层在当前仓库全局检索，优先复用已有的工具函数。
第三层优先使用语言自身的标准库。
第四层优先调用平台或浏览器自带的原生特性，比如用原生 dialog 替换弹窗库，用原生的 structuredClone 替换深拷贝依赖。
第五层如果必须调用外部能力，优先使用仓库里已安装的依赖，不引入新包。

最后如果确实要写新代码，只交付满足当前边界的最小实现。

项目地址：
https://t.co/xPcm2AYHyz

text:
太香了，今天逛博物馆，突然发现 Muse 免费拿来做历史教育，太好用了。

馆里有一组 1000 多年前吴越国的渔村布景。

河道、码头、帆船、捕鱼归来的渔民、村落、猪羊……本来只是一个静态的微缩场景。

哎，这不是白魔最牛逼的场景吗？

我拿手机沿着布景拍了一圈，直接扔给 Muse：

你把这个场景还原成真实世界，再按照我原来的镜头走位，做成一段视频。

它直接把原来 26 秒的视频拆成了 6 个分镜：

高空俯瞰村落和码头
→ 帆船停靠
→ 河道行船
→ 码头集市
→ 村落庭院
→ 街巷收尾

然后每个镜头重新生成 10 秒实景视频，最后拼成了整整 60 秒。

🔥最有意思的是：

我拍的是博物馆布景，它理解的却是这个布景背后的世界。

原来只能隔着玻璃看一眼的吴越渔村，现在船可以开起来，人可以捕鱼回来，整个村子真的活了。

以前博物馆告诉小孩：

1000 多年前的人是这样生活的。

现在直接演。

现在直接演。

text:
国庆七天假就是穷人和富人带娃最大的分水岭。

穷人的富养是带孩子到处旅游，富人的富养是给娃做多巴胺熔断。

这句话我前几年不信，直到去年看到周围孩子假期回来的状态，我彻底信了。普通家庭攒了大半年的钱带孩子逛景区逛乐园，聪明家庭关起门来给孩子搞多巴胺熔断。这是我近期看到的最震撼我的一篇育儿文章。

长假结束后的第一周，往往是无数家庭的灾难周。你一定见过这样的场景：孩子早上死活起不来，坐在书桌前眼神涣散写作业磨洋工，动不动就发脾气掉眼泪。老师在群里委婉地提醒孩子心还没收回来，家长在家里气得血压飙升。

为什么会这样？因为在过去的七天里，你花了大价钱，亲手把孩子的多巴胺阈值拉到了一个极其危险的高位。脑科学研究表明，多巴胺并不是快乐物质，它驱使我们去寻找新鲜刺激和即时满足。

普通家庭的假期是怎么过的？带孩子去人山人海的网红城市打卡，去声光电极度刺激的大型游乐园，吃各种高糖高热量的垃圾食品，在漫长的车程中为了让孩子安静，直接把手机和平板扔给他们刷短视频、打游戏。这些活动全都是高浓度短平快的多巴胺刺激。

当一个孩子的大脑连续七天习惯了100分的强刺激后，你让他突然回到只有20分刺激的课堂上，去面对黑板粉笔和枯燥的课本，他怎么可能坐得住？他的大脑会疯狂地抗议，觉得眼前的书本简直索然无味。这就是所谓的假期综合征，本质上是大脑的戒断反应。

而那些真正懂教育的聪明家庭，早就看透了这一点。他们深知保护孩子的专注力，比带他们去见识所谓的世面要重要一万倍。于是他们选择在长假进行多巴胺熔断，主动切断高刺激源，让孩子的大脑神经递质恢复到平静敏锐的初始状态。

很多父母有一种补偿心理：平时上班忙没时间陪孩子，好不容易放个长假，一定要带孩子去最贵的地方，以此来证明自己很爱孩子。但这真的是富养吗？你花了几千上万块钱，带着几岁的孩子在高速上堵车，在景区里看人头，打破了他们原有的睡眠规律和饮食习惯，孩子累得哇哇大哭，大人烦得大吼大叫。这种走马观花式的见世面，除了满足家长在朋友圈发九宫格的虚荣心，对孩子的认知提升微乎其微，反而造成了严重的感官超载。

真正的富养，从来不是物质上的无底线堆砌，而是认知上的高维引领。聪明的父母明白，这个时代最稀缺的资源不是信息，而是专注力。最顶级的快乐不是多巴胺的狂欢，而是内啡肽的沉淀。多巴胺是唾手可得的廉价快感，而内啡肽需要通过克服困难、深度思考、延迟满足才能获得。

如果你也想让孩子拥有强大的内核和持久的专注力，不妨在接下来的假期或周末，尝试以下三个熔断策略：

第一，允许孩子无聊，把时间留白。不要把孩子的假期安排得像赶通告一样密不透风。心理学发现，无聊是创造力的温床。当孩子抱怨“妈妈我好无聊”时，不要立刻塞给他一个玩具或电子屏幕，让他去发呆、去观察阳台上的蚂蚁、去拆解一个废旧的收音机。当外部刺激降到最低时，孩子内在的探索欲才会被真正激活。

第二，用内啡肽活动替代多巴胺娱乐。关掉电视，远离喧嚣的商场，带孩子去徒步爬山，去没有人工雕琢的自然环境里捡树叶、听鸟鸣，或者全家人围在一起，花三个小时拼完一个复杂的乐高，读完一本厚厚的人物传记。这些活动在开始时可能会有些枯燥，但完成后的成就感和内心的宁静，是任何游乐园都给不了的。

第三，捍卫底线，保持节日的稳定。长假不是放纵的借口，聪明的家庭即使在假期，也会严格守住两条底线：一是睡眠节律，二是阅读习惯。每天按时睡觉起床，每天保持至少半小时的深度阅读。这种看似刻板的规律，其实是在给孩子建立一种强大的秩序感。一个生活有秩序的孩子，内心才不会轻易失控。

在这个娱乐至死、算法算计人性的时代，毁掉一个孩子最快的方法，就是给他无限的高级刺激，让他对普通的日常事物丧失感知力。我们拼命赚钱，不是为了把孩子推向消费主义的陷阱，而是为了让他们有底气去拒绝那些廉价的诱惑。

这次长假，试着关上门，推掉不必要的社交和拥挤的旅行，陪孩子在安静的书桌前坐一坐，在无人的林荫道上走一走，帮孩子把多巴胺的阈值降下来，把专注力和感受力提上去。这才是父母能给孩子最顶级的富养，也是拉开孩子人生差距的真正分水岭。

text:
Took @karpathy's advice and started asking the agent for more visuals to walk through code. He's right. These models are so capable now.

Here I asked for a before-and-after HTML explainer on a PR that adds caching to our mobile app. Opus 5.5 gave a step-by-step diagram of the new flow, screenshots, and pointed me to the code worth reviewing. No skills being used here; it just knew what to show.

Saved a lot of time and let me align on architecture before opening GitHub

quotedTweet.text:
We'll be spending a lot more time trying to understand the outputs of language models. A few thoughts, tips & tricks:

Writing. Something I've had success with: Ask your LLM to explain something in ASD-STE100, it's a controlled language specification originally developed for aerospace maintenance documentation. LLMs well-versed in this language and it comes with heavy constraints on clean writing style that I often find a lot more readable. Sometimes I've tried to soften it a bit e.g. ask for "80% of the way to ASD-STE100" because the spec is quite stringent. But even better:

Diagrams / images. Instead of writing, ask your LLM to create a diagram. These can be a lot easier to process, parse, and understand. But even better:

Web pages. Ask for output "in HTML" to get a beautiful, interactive webpage. LLMs are getting really good at frontend and can create beautiful experiences, animations, etc. But even better:

Explainer videos. The output format I am most bullish on is fully custom / bespoke explainer videos generated on any arbitrary topic. Experiment with things like "Create a 3b1b style video explainer on X. Use my ElevenLabs API key for audio narration". (you'd need an API key for the latter or you can ask your LLM to find you decent free alternatives that use your local compute). This is actually starting to work!

In summary:
- As LLMs get better, they will do more and more of the legwork autonomously, and a lot more of our work will rise up the abstractions into oversight and understanding.
- Luckily, LLMs can help here too because as intelligence and code are increasingly abundant, you can ask for large, custom, discardable software artifacts (e.g. web apps, video explainers) that would have never made sense to create before. Push the boundaries here and you'll be surprised.

text:
不知道吧，你的 AI Agent 现在能从几乎任何网站扒数据了！ 🕷🔥

X、YouTube、Reddit、各种没 API 的论坛……研究、分析、监控要用的，基本全覆盖。

GitHub 上刚放出 3 个开源工具，直接给 Agent 装上这个超能力：

1️⃣. Agent-Reach
把 X、YouTube、Reddit、GitHub、B站、小红书整合到一处，一个 CLI，零 API 费用。
🔗 https://t.co/iwYLdY7FVN

2️⃣. Patchright Enhanced
用 Playwright 监听没有 API 的网站请求，脚本直接提取数据。
🔗 https://t.co/JTkpzK7hfI

3️⃣. Scrapling
通用网页抓取，任何网站都能啃。
🔗 https://t.co/p2aU69RvyZ

用法就一句话：你告诉它要什么数据 → 它写代码 → 抓回来 → 给你结果。

真实例子：

· "收集过去一个月 100 个 X 账号的帖子，告诉我哪些话题最火"
· "把 Reddit 和 YouTube 上这个产品的评论扒下来，总结主要槽点"

说白了，你的 Agent 从此能从互联网几乎任何角落提数据。这种自动化程度，搁不久前还不敢想。

#开源工具 #爬虫

text:
如果你想系统了解 AI，理清现在的技术全景，推荐你去翻翻 Hugging Face 上的排行榜。

很多人想认真了解 AI 时，容易被每天各种号称突破的新闻带偏，今天这个秒杀昨天那个登顶，看完依然不知道现在的真实格局到底是什么样。

Hugging Face 圈内习惯叫它抱抱脸，因为图标是个黄色笑脸。全球大部分团队开源出来的模型和数据，基本都会堆在这个网站上。

但它最有价值的地方，其实是各个细分领域的排行榜。

不管是大语言模型、代码生成，还是文本转语音、声音克隆、图像识别，甚至医疗问答或者防幻觉测试，都有专门的榜单。

翻这些榜单，能直接看到两个很关键的信息：
一个是当下在真实客观测试里，到底哪些开源模型真正排在前面。
另一个是每个细分方向到底在关注什么指标。比如看语音合成，你顺着榜单就会发现，大家比的不只是发音准不准，还要比首包延迟有多低、声音克隆相似度有多高。

不用去啃复杂的论文，多看几个不同任务的榜单，当前整个 AI 发展到了什么阶段、各家在攻克什么问题，脑子里自然就会有一张清晰的地图。

想找这些榜单，去 Hugging Face 的 Collections 页面搜索 leaderboard 就行，里面有整理好的汇总。

Hugging Face 合集入口：
https://t.co/Wp1LuPo3q9

今天分享一下之前找号商，开号买 Claude Max x20 的经验。但是，我问了一下价格就知道最近的 Claude 风控有多恐怖：

1. 独享账号 Max 20: 2000+一个。

2. 其他套餐就完全按照每日使用量来，一共四个档位。按照使用量的 token 对应的美金，来决定一个月的套餐。估计不能用多。

重点：下面的分享大家可以参考一下，最专业的号商提供服务，用户应该怎么样规避封号可能。

时效性跟有效性自行判断（我是在opus4.8发布后那短时间以及fable5发布后的那段时间一直在购买服务使用）！

先说结论：授权登录的环境以及避免多端（移动端、桌面端）使用才是最重要！！！IP、时区无所谓。另外商家支持拼车，这就说明了，同一个账号，多个ip根本没有问题！！！！

首先，我第一次买就是独享的 Max 20 账号，1800 一个月。我当时觉得多给几百服务费没问题，有售后，封号重新提供新号或者按比例退款。

当时开通的过程是，先给我一个新邮箱注册的 Pro 账号，用到限额爆炸，2天后如果没有触发风控就直接上 Max 20 订阅，那几天的 Pro 算是送了。

期间的所有登录授权，全是商家那边进行。我这边只需要在 Terminal 登录发送授权链接给他。

这里有一个关键点，每次他会提供一个错误的授权码给我测试一下，如果这个时候 Claude Code 显示403错误码，就证明网络无问题。敲黑板！！！他没有要求我任何关于电脑时区、IP！！！！然后就会再试一次登录。现在想起来，那就是根本不管使用 Claude Code的设备跟IP。

另外还有一个要求就是：不允许使用移动端，桌面端。

但是当时有一个特殊的情况，Claude 当时除了微软 office 套件，我想试试，商家也给我授权登录了。

还有一个小插曲，期间有一次号被封了。商家那边提到环境被污染了，需要重新测试。这里由此也能推断出来，授权登录环境是最重要的！！！

text:
It's happening. My wife told her friends how I set up a @bot to handle weekly meal planning and grocery shopping, saving 2-3 hours per week. 

They lean forward. "I want that! How do I get that?"

The AI factories are pitching travel agents, but mundane convenience seems like a killer feature to usher the Instagram crowd to Muse/Bot/Dot/etc.

Most people right now "use AI" the way I use a Swiss Army knife to lift the tab on a soda can, so everything she describes next lands like "The Turn" of a magic trick.

Every Sunday, "Sylvia-bot" sends 15 meal ideas and we choose 5-7 based on the week. It knows to assign the easy meals to the nights when our family calendar shows football practice. It knows to use ingredients 2-3 times in different ways, like a chef balancing COGS and flavors. It knows the components of a successful taco night.

We had years of weekly grocery orders for training, so it knows the brands, flavors, and sizes we prefer as a family. (I wonder how long it will take others to get to this point without the archive.)

We're still working on the idea that "grape tomatoes and cherry tomatoes are interchangeable" and "don't buy berries that aren't on sale!"

In 5 minutes, we approve the plan. It does the shopping on H-E-B, double-checks the pantry assumptions (e.g. soy sauce, spices, etc.), adds the kids' usual extras, and emails a clean PDF of every recipe for the week.

At the end of each week, we log our favorite to a 'recipe book' memory for future rotations.

For now, my wife will scan the cart (another 5 minutes) and confirm tomorrow's pickup window. Soon, I expect our Tesla will do the grocery run on its own.

到晚饭时，餐桌对面或许坐着一个心智成熟、认知同频的她，也或许没有。不过，都不重要了。睡前，你随手拿起一本书读着，几分钟后，困意袭来。你放下书，很快进入了睡眠。没有惊天动地的成功，只是一切都走上了正轨。如此，足矣。

Cloudflare 刚发布了新功能，但我看了看价格，忍不住想笑。

他们出了个给 AI 用的 Web Search API，把 Ceramic、Linkup、Exa 全部打包了。重点是： 别人做中间商都是为了赚差价。 

Cloudflare 做中间商：“原价给你，我一分钱中间费不加，甚至你想用自己的 key 也行。”

很多人纳闷：它图啥？它图你不用再去充三家公司的信用卡； 它图你写 Agent 时随手一行 https://t.co/J73lotSrPY.websearch； 它图你所有的 AI 流量都必须从它的 Gateway 走过。

表面是做 API，底层是在吞噬整个 Agent 基础设施生态。什么时候把做产品做成“你离不开我，哪怕我今天免费”，才叫降维打击。

text:
胖东来就是科幻片。

Bank of America派商业间谍从北卡飞到河南许昌调查过，出过一份报告，里面90%是游客特意来打开买的（包括代购和网红跟风狗）。

许昌本地每年人均可支配收入35000块钱，这种穷逼城市是没多少人能买得起胖东来的产品的。

胖东来主力就是熟食，实际上等于一个大型美食城， 进去什么炒菜炖肉烤肉烤鸡一顿吃，点几个水果大榴莲给你切好处理好了，价格比市场高1倍，

吃完再带几大瓶原粮食白酒、无农药茶叶、动物奶油大蛋糕、保质期3天的大瓶橙汁、正宗东北大米，带一堆小零食、大麻花、酱牛肉、酱肘子，再带一堆什么非转基因大豆油、卫生巾、湿巾等等容易暴雷的产品，拉一大车后备箱两三千块钱的柴米油盐回家。

实际上中国的Sam's Club就是中国的wholefoods，绝对健康，极度健康，有机且难吃，

胖东来就是中国的Sam's Club+trader joe，兼具了健康有机和重油重盐重酱重味精和特别好吃，本质上是更符合中国味蕾的、不需要会员费的精致版wholefoods。

这是胖东来目前当今此时此刻的运营模式。

text:
I’m tired of OpenAI pretending it listens to users while ignoring the people who actually point out what’s wrong.

Here are some real questions from real users:
- Why is ChatGPT still on GPT-5.6 instead of 6.1?
- Why does a “weekly” limit only start after your first message, so it can effectively become 10+ days?
- Why does a reset restart that whole 7-day wait, while Claude doesn’t do this?
- Why can a confirmed bug burn your weekly limit, then support closes the case, gives no compensation, no fix update, and keeps sending canned AI replies?

The last one is just one example from my own experience. I reported it two months ago, OpenAI confirmed the bug, and I still got no compensation or even an update on whether it was fixed. I seriously doubt my case is unique. Anyone who has tried getting a real issue through support probably knows what I’m talking about.

And Tibo, if hundreds of replies are piling in under your comment, how are you realistically supposed to notice the answer from the one person you actually asked?

That’s what annoys me about this. OpenAI needs to either seriously fix how it collects feedback and handles support, or stop acting like replies like this mean they’re listening.
I’m not saying Anthropic is any better internally. But at least they’re not all over X asking people for feedback they obviously aren’t going listen.

一个冷知识，生孩子的性别不是开盲盒，而是可以选择的。所以你们觉得男女比例非常的失衡，其实是人为选择的，而不是杀婴和堕胎。
Y 精子游得快，但寿命短；X 精子游得慢，但寿命长。
所以说，如果卵子已经在等着了，此时精子来了，那么就会生男孩。

text:
非农爆了个大冷门，美股却创了新高——这个市场看的从来不是现实，是预期。

周五出的数据：9月新增就业2.9万，预期可是8.4万，直接膝斩。失业率升到4.2%，7月数据还被下修成了负增长。

按常理想，就业这么拉胯，股市不得跌个狗吃屎？

结果纳指涨1.19%，直接历史新高。标普、英伟达跟着新高，特斯拉一天干了4.65%。

为啥？因为市场赌的从来不是"经济好不好"，是"美联储敢不敢加息"。

数据越冷，加息越没戏——10月加息概率一周前还64%，数据一出直接掉到20%上下。

靴子落地，资金反而松了口气，冲进去抢跑。

所以炒股炒的从来不是"现在怎么样"，是"接下来会怎么样"。

数据是后视镜，预期才是方向盘。2.9万这个数字本身不重要，重要的是它杀死了加息预期。

利空出尽是利好，利好出尽……你懂的。

明天应该又是满盘绿！

We’ve all been hearing that subscriptions are cheaper than APIs, but I’d never seen the exact number.

So yesterday, I took several popular plans and burned a slice of their weekly allowance on purpose. I logged every model call and priced those calls at the vendor’s public API list price.

While I couldn't test all subscription levels: 

According to OpenAI, their monthly allowance is now directly proportional to the subscription price:

- Plus ($20/mo) = the reference OpenAI monthly allowance
- Pro 100 ($100/mo) = 5x monthly allowance - tested
- Pro 200 ($200/mo) = 10x monthly allowance (just downgraded from 20x)

For Claude, their Max 20x is subsidized twice as much:

- Pro ($20/mo) = the reference Claude monthly allowance
- Max 5x ($100/mo) = 5x monthly allowance
- Max 20x ($200/mo) = 20x monthly allowance (not 10x) - tested

According to Meta, for Muse Code:

- Everyday Usage ($5/mo) = the reference Muse monthly allowance
- High Usage ($15/mo) = 5x monthly allowance (not 3x) - tested
- Power Usage ($50/mo) = 20x monthly allowance (not 10x)

What does all this mean? (1/4) 🧵

text:
Important advice: deliberately rethink every previous concept of how things should be done.

Some thoughts, tips, and realizations:

1. Specializations are collapsing. Come to terms with and take advantage of this reality. The person who used to be an engineer is now also a data scientist, a content creator, designer, marketer, and whatever else they want to be. Deliberately expand in as many directions as you can and become great at them (scope up vs just speeding up)

2. The average person with access to tokens can now do the work of a data scientist who used to cost $500,000 a year. Seriously, this is fucking crazy. This opens up an entirely new world. Take advantage of it (also everyone else will also realize this over time).

3. 99% of what's created is now slop. Be aggressively anti-slop and you will absolutely stand out.

4. Trying is nearly free. Automating is nearly free. My mind still sometimes lives in the world from 12 months ago where an idea automatically is attached to a certain amount of time or effort. Both of these have collapsed to close to zero (or just token cost), I therefore try and experiment with *any and all* ideas with potential and have needed to retrain my brain for this constantly.

5. Tokens are a career and growth accelerant. Find ways to get cheap access to tokens, or free tokens. Extremely important, and actually an entire design space, use your imagination.

6. It's never been easier to both stand out but also fall behind. 10x, 100x "people" exist more than ever (maybe 1,000x). Outlier power users of AI, many who you see here on X. Feels like we are in a window of time, a window of opportunity while all of this is still early, to take advantage of it. 

7. Local computing is (or will be) dead for 99% of work. Local was built for a world where work was bounded by the physical presence of its author, but this is no longer true. You can and should do infinite work in parallel or zero, it doesn't matter anymore. Cloud agents enable this at scale and in any computing environment, I predict cloud agent usage will 1000x over the next 12 months and optionality and accessibility will 100x. Plan for this world, take advantage of the possibilities.

8. Building on #7, you can give an agent it's own computer, and it's own identity. You can then give an agent with it's own computer it's own computer. You can give that agent with it's own computer with it's own computer, *it's* own computer. These agents are smarter than any human in history and you have access to as many as you'd like. Think about this for a moment.

After 14 years in this industry (tech) today is the most exciting time ever and nothing else feels even close.

quotedTweet.text:
#8 一图一策略，我把传奇短线交易员Bit浪浪的策略弄出来了🥲🤓

Bit浪浪从借钱吃饭到赚4000万收手，长期实盘排行榜第一名那位，他的超细节的交易方法无码公开，看完先掌握三成功力，这个一定收藏好！！

他说做交易只要遵循他的交易逻辑和仓位管理规则，那交易这件事就能成，首先说交易逻辑，我们要先明确币种的阶段位置，币种从冷到热一般会经历六个阶段，每个阶段会对应不同的介入手法。

开始启动，行情启动就是阶段一！

浪浪就有六个优中选优的介入位置，他说除此六个位置之外的任何一笔交易都属于犯病，一个币往往会以突破一个大级别的震荡结构。

肯定要有一个目标位，目标位有可能是压力位，也有可能是整数位等关键位置，在到达目标位之前往往会经历一个或多个小分歧，这些小分歧就是阶段二，行情会在上涨和小分歧间不断地上行！！

趋势行情启动之后，主升浪在到达目标位之后，就会产生一次比较大的大分歧，震荡持续的时间会比较长，这个大分歧就是阶段三，大分歧结束之后，如果有二波拉升，走二波的前后就是阶段四，二波会延续前面的主升浪，中间也会产生分歧，直到行情到了它最终的目标位之后见顶，形成阶段五，之后整个行情就算进入末期下跌，再到进入震荡，这里就是阶段六！

但是市场在这时候，其实还一直有多头在进场，很难确定什么时候能真正拐头向下，就很容易被向上的反弹或者插针打损！！这六个阶段里，阶段三和五是要做逆势交易，阶段六是因为波动太没有规律比较难把握，这三个阶段难度都比较大，不太建议各位去做。

最绝佳最容易赚钱的机会是阶段一和四。

浪浪说这两个阶段是任何时候都要满仓梭哈的位置，阶段二是其次，在阶段一二四，交易的逻辑和介入位置是先确定大级别趋势和阶段，比如日线或者小时线，然后判断上方的盈利空间够不够大，也就是距离价格最容易出现停止和反转的位置幅度有多大，最后是切换到小级别图表，找顺势的企稳拐点！！

Dot voice: what we're fixing ⚒️ 

We're hearing lots of great feedback on Dot voice:

1. It takes too long to connect or fails entirely (5-6 rings)
2. The phone call UX: some people love it, some don't
3. No way to see transcript or summary
4. Says "Checking" too much
5. Sometimes goes quiet and does not give updates

Here's what we're doing next:

1. Making connection fast and reliable
2. Keeping the phone call UX for now, but instant
3. Adding transcript and summaries to the UI
4. Adding more variance to "Checking" (eventually will remove it for fast questions)
5. Adding more regular updates

Our goal is for Dot voice to become the chief-of-staff you can delegate any task to, hands-free.

What did we miss? Please keep the feedback coming!

quotedTweet.text:
FINAL THOUGHTS ON THIS PAST WEEK:

I've been a Hawkeye fan for more than 40 years, and I'm sitting in my garage close to midnight on Saturday with a drink, watching Caitlin Clark highlights on YouTube and feeling proud as hell.

Which is kind of strange when you think about it.

Caitlin and the Fever were eliminated from the playoffs this week.

Iowa just got rolled by Ohio State.

Normally, that sounds like a pretty miserable few days to be an Iowa fan.

But somehow, it doesn't feel that way.

College GameDay came back to Iowa City.

Nike turned Caitlin's shoe launch into an event on the Pentacrest, building a temporary basketball court right next to the GameDay stage.

Caitlin came home and was the guest picker.

She picked Iowa, of course. 😅

And then came the Wave.

After the first quarter, 70,000 people inside Kinnick turned toward the children's hospital.

The cameras went up to the windows, where the kids and their families were waving down at the stadium.

And standing up there with them, waving back at Kinnick, was Caitlin Clark.

Maybe the most famous athlete the University of Iowa has ever produced.

One of the most recognizable athletes in the world.

And somehow, in that moment, she wasn't a global superstar making an appearance.

She was a Hawkeye who came home.

One of ours.

That's what I've been thinking about tonight.

At Iowa, we're probably never going to measure our fandom by a trophy case full of national championships.

That doesn't mean winning doesn't matter.

Of course it fucking matters. 😂

I wanted the Fever to keep playing.

I wanted Iowa to beat the hell out of Ohio State.

Losses hurt. Bad seasons piss us off. We bitch about coaches, officials, play calling, recruiting and everything else sports fans bitch about.

But the older I get, the more I realize that being a Hawkeye has never really been dependent on any of those things.

It's deeper than wins and losses.

I've never been part of another collegiate fan base, so maybe others feel the same way about theirs.

But Hawkeye fandom has always felt like a family to me.

In Iowa City, it's everywhere. You can feel it walking down the street.

But I live in Minnesota.

And I can't tell you how many times I've been walking through a store wearing an Iowa shirt and heard some complete stranger yell:

"LET'S GO HAWKS!"

And immediately, you know.

You're one of us.

A 6'4"-6'5" kid commits to Iowa women's basketball, someone I've never met and probably never will, and my first thought isn't just, "Great pickup."

It's:

WELCOME TO THE FAMILY.

That's what being a Hawkeye feels like.

Players come and go.

Coaches come and go.

Seasons come and go.

There are incredible wins we'll talk about for the rest of our lives, and absolutely brutal losses we'd prefer to erase from our memories.

But the Tigerhawk remains.

The people remain.

The family remains.

Wins are something Hawkeyes celebrate together.

Losses are something Hawkeyes suffer together.

But being a Hawkeye?

That doesn't change.

So yeah.

The Fever lost.

The Hawks got rolled.

And somehow I'm sitting here tonight feeling more proud than ever to say:

I'm an Iowa Hawkeye.

Always have been.

Always will be.

💛🖤

GO HAWKS.

text:
Here are 9 things we found in our 2K27 research:
***Visuals and full breakdown is on our blog, this is an extensive breakdown so we encourage you to follow the link to get the whole picture, we also want to highlight #9.
https://t.co/Zswv4FvlCf

**1. Adrenaline affects shooting.**
Each boost spent subtracts 10 points from the rating used for that shot. An 85 becomes 75, 65, then 55 with none left, before other modifiers.

**2. Hot zones change the shot rating.**
Cold: −2. Neutral: 0. Hot: +2. Lethal: +4. Those are rating points, not extra percentage points of makes.

**3. Being hot or cold matters separately.**
Frozen: −6. Cold: −3. Warm: +3. Hot or Takeover: +6 to the ratings in that skill group. This basic adjustment doesn’t boost Speed, Agility, Strength or Vertical.

**4. Some NBA roster players have a hidden contest advantage.**
Unfazed reduces contest strength. Examples include Curry and Lillard at 12%, Luka and Bird at 16%. That doesn’t mean 16% more makes.

**5. Certain shooting badge bonuses share a +30 cap.**
Their qualifying Bronze through Legend bonuses are +4, +8, +11, +15 and +19. Two qualifying +19 bonuses reach +30, not +38. This cap doesn’t cover every badge effect.

**6. Yes, getting taller above 7 feet can make threes harder.**
The researched height adjustment has no cut at 7′0″ or below, then roughly 7% at 7′1″, 12% at 7′2″ and 20% at 7′3″.

A 50% starting chance becomes about 46.5%, 44% or 40% from that factor alone.

**7. Meter off gives 10% more timing room.**
A 30 ms jumper or layup window becomes 33 ms. This researched bonus doesn’t apply to the skill-dunk meter.

**8. Active takeover can widen the window further.**
Shot Artist and Calibrated give +50% for threes and shots beyond 20 feet, or +45% for ordinary mid-range shots. With meter off, a qualifying 30 ms window becomes 49.5 ms. The ability has to be active.

**9. Low stamina lowers effective ratings.**
With longer-term fatigue fresh, the shooting penalty begins below 61.11% of ordinary yellow capacity. With both blue extensions, that’s 43.65% of the whole expanded meter.

An 85 Three-Point plays as about 83 at half ordinary capacity, 79 at a quarter and 32 at empty, from stamina alone. The last 10% of ordinary capacity adds a steep extra penalty.

text:
I don't understand why everyone isn't doing this yet.

Anthropic's own Claude Code docs show how to run a whole team of Claudes, while Opus 5.5 only touches the plan and the merge

the whole idea: agent teams in Claude Code

one lead, separate teammates in their own context windows, one shared task list, and they message each other directly

the lead: Opus 5.5 on high, splits the work, writes the tasks, merges at the end
the builders: Sonnet 5.5, one owns client/, one owns api/, never the same file
the adversary: Fable 5.1, never writes code, only shows up at three points:

→ before an interface locks: do both sides agree on the contract?
→ when a test fails twice: is it fixed or just hidden?
→ before a task is marked done: what breaks it?

Sonnet 5.5 builds. Fable 5.1 attacks. Opus 5.5 merges

Jev engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to Jev in under half a second, and the team only argues about the ones that split

turn it on, then start the team in plain English:

"Spawn three teammates: ux and backend on Sonnet, an adversary on Fable"

- the full team
> Opus 5.5 on high leads the session
> ux on Sonnet 5.5, owns client/
> backend on Sonnet 5.5, owns api/
> adversary on Fable 5.1, owns nothing, reviews everything
> shared task list with file locking, direct messages, no lead in the middle

paste the team and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Set up agent teams for this repo:

1. In ~/.claude/settings.json add CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 under env and set effortLevel to high

2. In ~/.claude/agents, draft three subagent definitions for the teammates

> ux and backend with model: sonnet, each limited to its own folder
> adversary with model: fable and read-only tools, whose only job is attacking contracts, repeated test failures and done claims
> Skip any that already exist and list them

3. Add a TaskCompleted hook that blocks completion until the adversary signs off, and one rule to CLAUDE.md: no two teammates edit the same file

4. Find anything that would override this (CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE, CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL). Report it, change nothing

Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go."

↳ https://t.co/WM2ACfWw8B

哈佛长达三十年的人群追踪研究，戳破了绝大多数人的努力假象。真正拉开人与人差距的，根本不是熬夜、体力劳累这种低级吃苦，这些只有消耗、没有复利。

真正能让人跃迁的，是主动给自己找的三类高级痛苦：突破认知的成长之苦、直面批评修正自我的摩擦之苦、长期低回报坚持的延迟满足之苦。

判断吃苦值不值很简单：是否主动选择、能否突破边界、能否迭代认知。就像芒格，把人生极致苦难，最终熬成了顶级认知。我个人觉得延迟满足感的能力培养实在太重要了，你在很多成功人士身上都能看到这一特质！

Simple Algorithmic Theory of Subjective Beauty, Novelty, Surprise, Interestingness, Attention, Curiosity, Creativity, Art, Science, Music, Jokes

Jürgen SCHMIDHUBER

Abstract

In this summary of previous work, I argue that data becomes temporarily interesting by itself to some self-improving, but computationally limited, subjective observer once he learns to predict or compress the data in a better way, thus making it subjectively more “beautiful.” Curiosity is the desire to create or discover more non-random, non-arbitrary, “truly novel,” regular data that allows for compression progress because its regularity was not yet known. This drive maximizes “interestingness,” the first derivative of subjective beauty or compressibility, that is, the steepness of the learning curve. It motivates exploring infants, pure mathematicians, composers, artists, dancers, comedians, yourself, and recent artificial systems.

I finished 1st 🥇 on my age group and 5th in the male category.

I failed my ambitious goal of sub-60 but I was very happy with my race. And I have a nice goal to chase for the next few months.

All the staff at the Hyrox venue knew us! I even talked to the manager of Hyrox Turkey/Dubai/Greece. His name his Mustafa and he let my wife inside the athlete zone to shot videos for our YouTube channel.

It’s my first Hyrox and the energy is insane. Everybody is fit, sexy and topless. There’s a DJ and MC so it feels like a gym-club in Bali. No surprise this sport is growing so much!

This little experiment is engraved in my head.

The last 2 weeks have been surreal. Getting paid $112,000 to race, receiving a fancy car at my hotel lobby, getting recognized by a lot of people, my first race… so many things to process!

I want to thank my sponsors who made this possible:

- https://t.co/U5ahUBM08z by @higgsfield (10 spots!)
- https://t.co/gu76BTYuz2 by @kelvincobanaj
- https://t.co/pLgrGEC7Ag by @notgokgreen

- https://t.co/myeIzGZvX0 by @peptideconfiden
- https://t.co/pWuPj9uUz6 by @jayhoovy (🍑)

I want to thank my wife for always trusting in me and pushing me to try whatever crosses my mind.

I want to thank all of you who supported the idea, online and offline.

And I want to thank me for believing in myself. I was lost for so long. I felt misunderstood by people thinking I was weird for trying all kind of experiments. In the end I just want to have fun, and I’m incredibly grateful that my hard work has finally compounded and now I can play and get paid for it.

Ok I’m a bit emotional now, and I’m getting late for my second race of the day with my wife. This one is just for fun. Woohoo!
